reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it actively promotes purchasing StrongBlock nodes by presenting recurring node income of up to $55,000 per month and urging viewers to enter early, while repeatedly describing the purchase as potentially highly profitable. The speaker gives operational instructions for buying nodes, says he purchased more himself, and frames participation as a time-sensitive opportunity, despite acknowledging volatility and possible losses. The risk warnings qualify the claims but do not remove the video's central solicitation to purchase paid nodes for unusually large passive returns.

people will potentially be getting $55,000 in a single month from being in here
if you really do decide, Hey, this is really looking cool. This is something that I want to jump into
I do think that overall, it's going to be a good purchase
You'll also get access to all of my videos up to two to three days earlier than everyone else

opening.argument: The presentation is materially qualified rather than deceptive. It expressly warns that crypto is risky, says the token price can plummet, acknowledges volatility, and describes the projected $55,000 monthly figure as speculation rather than a promise. It also tells viewers to do their own research before entering and explains that maintenance and gas fees reduce the apparent return. A conditional, risk-heavy discussion of possible outcomes is better understood as investment commentary than as a guaranteed-income solicitation.

citations.quote: All things in crypto are super risky, but these things, even more so because, you know, the price can really plummet
So again, this is all speculation. I'm not saying that that's going to happen or StrongBlock is
do your research first
you do have to pay fees to run your notes

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes the most attractive hypothetical while minimizing the qualifications surrounding it. The $55,000 figure is expressly presented as speculation, and the speaker warns of volatility and substantial losses. Saying that viewers may consider entering does not convert a conditional risk discussion into a guarantee, especially where the speaker identifies fees and tells viewers to research first.

citations.quote: So again, this is all speculation.
the price can definitely be volatile
there's risk of losing 80, 90, 70 percent of your funds

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Risk disclaimers do not erase the central message. The speaker still describes node ownership as producing recurring daily tokens, calls the purchase good overall, and urges early participation because rewards may decrease. Calling the upside speculation does not prevent the presentation from using unusually large projected returns to encourage entry.

I do think that overall, it's going to be a good purchase
The earlier you are in a lot of this stuff, a lot of times the better

opening.argument: The video's structure is an explanatory walkthrough of how StrongBlock operates and how the creator evaluates it, not a claim that viewers will certainly profit. It explains the token requirement, node reward calculation, compounding concept, fees, possible future chains, and declining rewards. The speaker repeatedly presents his own experience and perspective, including what he purchased and what he has earned, giving viewers information to assess rather than certifying the product as safe or successful.

citations.quote: the quick overview over the quick synopsis about how it works is you purchase 10 StrongBlock tokens
if we take a look at how many strong tokens I've made so far in the first 20 days
you do have to pay fees to run your notes
that's you know my perspective

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats explanation of the mechanics as an instruction to buy. But describing how tokens, nodes, compounding, and fees work is precisely what allows viewers to evaluate the proposal. The speaker identifies his discussion as his perspective and gives personal results, rather than representing that every viewer will receive the same outcome.

citations.quote: the quick overview over the quick synopsis about how it works
that's what I'm really looking at. That's my perspective on this

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The operational explanation is not neutral merely because it contains mechanics. It tells viewers how to purchase nodes, highlights daily rewards and compounding, and repeatedly frames early participation as advantageous. Personal testimony and a disclaimer about perspective can make a promotion more relatable without changing its solicitation function.

citations.quote: you're able to go over to the website here and purchase a node
you can actually take those 10 tokens that you can get that you can claim and compound that into another note
The earlier you are in a lot of this stuff, a lot of times the better

opening.argument: The evidence describes a purchaseable crypto product with stated costs, maintenance obligations, and transaction fees, which is compatible with ordinary commerce rather than an inherently fraudulent mechanism. The speaker explains that users purchase tokens and nodes, notes that gas and maintenance costs apply, and even advises consolidating transactions to reduce fees. The supplied material does not establish a guaranteed return, a downline, a credential request, or a requirement to recruit others; projected appreciation is conditional and expressly speculative.

citations.quote: you purchase 10 StrongBlock tokens and you're able to go over to the website here and purchase a node
it does cost maintenance. So you need to pay the maintenance fees
do it all in one multi purchase because when you do it that way you're going to reduce your gas fees
So again, this is all speculation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution calls the purchase a scam mechanism without identifying evidence of deception in the transaction itself. The discussion openly identifies what must be purchased and what costs apply, including maintenance and gas. A paid product or service can be promoted without being fraudulent, and conditional forecasts do not establish a guaranteed-return scheme.

citations.quote: you do have to pay fees to run your notes
the gas fees is really where it adds up purchasing these nodes
this is all speculation

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Disclosure of fees does not make the underlying offer ordinary or reliable. The video still links node purchases to recurring token income, encourages multiple nodes, and uses projected five-figure monthly earnings as an inducement. The absence of a downline or credential request is not decisive when the relevant concern is paid nodes marketed for passive returns.

With that node, you're going to be able to earn 0.1 StrongTokens every single day.
